claims.text: Machine learning–guided electrochemical dealloying of a multicomponent noble-metal HEA precursor will produce three-dimensional nanoframeworks.
The resulting three-dimensional nanoframeworks will be stable under operating conditions.
The resulting nanoframeworks will have tunable, hierarchical porosity and increased surface area.
The resulting nanoframeworks will retain a uniform, precisely tunable multi-element distribution.
A suitable precursor contains both noble and sacrificial metals in near-equimolar proportions.
A machine-learning model can identify suitable settings for precursor composition, electrolyte chemistry, applied potential, temperature, and processing time.
Optimizing those process variables can maximize porosity and elemental-distribution uniformity.
Anodic potentials near the dissolution threshold of the less noble metals enable preferential removal of those metals.
The dealloying process can be conducted at a controlled temperature of approximately 25–60 °C.
An appropriately selected electrolyte preferentially dissolves the more reactive alloy components.
Selective dissolution of less noble species under controlled electrochemical conditions forms a self-supporting, ligand-free three-dimensional network of the remaining elements.
Machine learning can correlate processing parameters with textural and compositional outcomes.
These correlations accelerate the search for conditions that combine selective dissolution with uniform retention of multiple metals.
The nanoframework's increased surface area and tuned elemental distribution will produce superior catalytic performance.
Conventional trial-and-error or simple parametric studies may fail to produce or reproducibly yield compositionally uniform three-dimensional nanoframeworks.
Selective dealloying becomes less effective when constituent-metal reactivities are insufficiently distinct.
Conflicting kinetic effects can hinder uniform pore formation.
Evidence is limited regarding scale-up and nanoframework stability under different reaction conditions.
